prayerExcerpt.en-US: If we do not love penitence for its own sake, let us love it on account of our sins; for we should "work out our salvation in fear and trembling."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Se não amamos a penitência por si mesma, amemo-la por causa de nossos pecados; pois devemos "operar a nossa salvação com temor e tremor."

meta.face: A man of about sixty, burned a deep bronze by the sun, with a LEAN face whose HIGH, BROAD, FLAT cheekbones run in a straight line across it — NARROW eyes that SLANT gently DOWN at the outer corners, dark and sorrowful, under thick, level black-and-grey brows, a LONG, THIN, very STRAIGHT nose, SUNKEN cheeks below the cheekbones, a thin mouth; long, unkempt black-and-grey hair to the shoulders; a LONG, dense, rough black-and-grey beard to the breast; the gaze penitent and humble, a little lowered.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The book tells a recluse in the ruins of an old tower near Villafranca, a league from Nice, girded with an iron chain, living on bread and dates, who foretold the Lombard raids and healed the arm of a Lombard who raised his sword against him; its engraving shows a bearded, long-haired recluse seated before a ruined arch while soldiers approach. Wikipedia, after Gregory of Tours, places the tower on Cap Ferrat, called Cap Saint-Hospice, and gives him an Egyptian origin by tradition. The lean face with the flat, high cheekbones and the down-slanting eyes is our choice.
